# Task M-09: a song search waits for a download slot instead of giving up

**Phase:** maintenance · **Depends on:** none · **Suggested tier:** Sonnet subagent · **Estimated size:** S/M

## Goal

Found on `ch01` (2026-10-10): ten songs added at once each got a `SongSearch` (search on add, then by hand through `POST /command`). Six finished **"Cancelled — No free download slot"** (`src/Wondarr.Core/Searching/SongSearchService.cs` ~line 470: `grab && accepted > 0 && trigger != Manual && !HasFreeSlotAsync`) — the accepted candidates were thrown away, and the song waited for the 6-hourly Missing Search. A user who adds songs expects each to be fetched as slots free up.

## Deliverables

1. Read how download slots, the queue (`QueueStatus.Queued` etc.) and the Missing Search's batch loop ("waited for a slot before it got here") work, and pick the simplest correct behaviour, in this order of preference:
   - **(a)** if the queue can hold a grab that has not started yet and starts it when a slot frees (a local `Queued` state the download manager drains), grab the best accepted candidate into it instead of cancelling;
   - **(b)** otherwise, a `SongSearch` command (any trigger) waits for a free slot (re-checking, at most `search.slot_wait_minutes`, default 30), reports "Waiting for a download slot" as its progress, then grabs the best accepted candidate that is still not blocklisted; after the wait it ends `Cancelled — still no free download slot after N min` and the song stays wanted.
   Whichever you choose: a wait must not hold the Soulseek search budget or a database transaction, and must honour cancellation (shutdown, a user cancelling the command). Say in the done-report which you chose and why, and whether `MissingSearch`'s own loop needs any change.
2. Candidates already accepted by the run are what is grabbed — no second search.
3. The Activity → Queue / Tasks page shows the waiting state (whatever text the chosen design produces).
4. Docs: `website/src/content/docs/sources/soulseek.md` or `library/adding-songs.md` — one sentence on what happens when all download slots are busy. `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` → `### Fixed`.

## Allowed paths

- `src/Wondarr.Core/Searching/**`, `src/Wondarr.Core/Sources/**` (queue/download manager), `src/Wondarr.Core/Jobs/**` (only if the command progress needs it), `src/Wondarr.Core/Configuration/**` (the new option)
- `tests/Wondarr.Core.Tests/**`, `tests/Wondarr.Api.Tests/**`
- `website/src/content/docs/library/adding-songs.md`, `website/src/content/docs/sources/soulseek.md`, `website/src/content/docs/reference/configuration.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

## Constraints

- AGENTS.md external limits (Soulseek ≤ 2 outstanding searches, 30 per 4 min) unchanged.
- The executor runs at most 3 commands at once: a design that parks three waiting SongSearch commands in all three workers would starve every other command — avoid it (this is why (a) is preferred; with (b), release the worker while waiting or cap waiting searches).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `dotnet build -warnaserror`; Core, Sources, Api tests one at a time — green.
2. Tests: with every slot busy, a search with accepted candidates does not end `Cancelled — No free download slot`; when a slot frees, the grab happens (the song gets a queue item) without a new search; cancellation while waiting; other commands still run while searches wait.

## Done-report

Use the format in `docs/build/WORKER_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`.
